extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and professional video game writers, narrative designers, and game industry writing teams
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, professional guidance for writing narrative, dialogue, documentation, tutorials, and voice content for video games, plus career and team-working advice for both novice and veteran writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story and narrative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers story and narrative elements relevant to games (how to craft game stories and integrate narrative into gameplay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book covers story and narrative elements as part of the core craft of writing for video games; includes principles of narrative design and ways to innovate in game narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing playable, performable dialogue for characters and in-game interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses dialogue across chapters including recording studio considerations and barks (short voice lines); practical writing tips from industry pros inform how to write dialogue suitable for performance and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing proper documentation that game teams expect from writers (design documents, scripts, spreadsheets, casting sides, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3 and appendices provide examples and formats; the book emphasizes documentation as an essential deliverable for communication with design, art, and engineering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game Script Formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct formatting conventions for game scripts (screenplay and modified screenplay formats shown in appendices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2 and Appendices A and B contain script samples—CALL OF JUAREZ screenplay format and BRATZ modified screenplay format—demonstrating accepted industry formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing instructions, helptext, walkthroughs, and manuals (Text to train the player)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing clear instructions, help text, walkthroughs and manuals intended to teach or guide the player.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4 frames such text as 'Text to Train the Player'—focus on clarity, usability, and player learning rather than literary flourish; includes writing for in-game UI and manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Tutorials: Write 'Start' to Start
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing and writing in-game tutorials to introduce mechanics and get players started effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5 emphasizes practical tutorial-writing techniques—how to teach by doing, sequencing, and keeping tutorial text concise and actionable ('Write "Start" to Start').

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical techniques for productivity: Getting the work done
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and habits for being productive and efficient as a game writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 6 provides productivity techniques from industry practitioners focused on output, time management, and being an efficient part of a team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborating with art, design, and engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices for cross-disciplinary collaboration and communication with artists, designers, and engineers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7 discusses how writers fit into teams and how to communicate narrative needs and constraints to other disciplines to ensure implementable narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for AAA games
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations and approaches specific to writing for large-scale, high-budget (AAA) game projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 8 ('Playing in the Big Leagues') covers scale, processes, and expectations unique to AAA development teams and pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for Indie Games
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches tailored to small teams and indie production constraints and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9 addresses differences in scope, flexibility, and creative control when writing for independent games.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game writing remotely: How to pay the rent working from home
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices and logistics for remote game writing and freelance/contract work from home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 10 gives guidance on remote workflows, communication, self-management and sustaining income while working remotely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game writing on staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and responsibilities for writers hired as staff within studios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11 contrasts staff positions with contract/freelance roles, detailing integration into studio processes and team structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping localization in mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing and writing narrative and UI text with localization and global distribution considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 12 ('When Game Narrative Travels Abroad') emphasizes clear, localization-friendly phrasing and collaboration with localization teams to avoid cultural and technical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writers in the recording studio
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing for and working in voice recording sessions and related audio production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 13 covers studio practices, working with actors/directors, casting sides, and how to prepare text (timing, barks, context) for recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for existing licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapting voice and narrative to established licensed IP and respecting constraints of external properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14 discusses working within the restrictions and expectations of licensed franchises, including tone, canonical consistency, and stakeholder approval processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for new IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating original intellectual property: building worlds, lore, and characters from scratch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 15 addresses inventing new IP, establishing voice and lore, and documentation practices to support expansion and cross-team use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script doctoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics for revising, improving, and repairing existing scripts and narrative assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 16 ('Script Doctoring') provides techniques for analyzing weak spots, proposing fixes, and collaborating with teams to integrate changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing compelling game characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for creating memorable, believable game characters that serve gameplay and story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 17 focuses on character goals, motivations, arcs, and how to make characters compelling within interactive contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring philosophies: We can do better
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and critiques of hiring practices for game writing roles and how teams can improve recruitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 18 examines studio hiring philosophies and suggests better approaches to finding and evaluating writing talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: If it works, break it: Game narrative tropes and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding common narrative tropes in games and strategies for innovating or subverting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 19 encourages critical use of tropes and offers ways to innovate in game narrative while remaining effective for players.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script samples and appendix formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete script examples and deliverable formats (screenplay, modified screenplay) for reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A (CALL OF JUAREZ screenplay format) and Appendix B (BRATZ modified screenplay format) provide ready examples; helpful for formatting submissions and internal documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barks and task spreadsheet (technical deliverables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizing short voice lines ('barks') and task tracking with spreadsheets for implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix C contains a 'BARKS AND TASK SPREADSHEET' illustrating how to structure barks and related metadata for engineering and audio teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting sides for recording sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing casting sides and materials for auditions and actor direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix D ('CASTING SIDES FOR CALL OF JUAREZ') shows examples of how to format and present lines for casting and studio direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to break into the video game industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice and strategies for finding jobs and starting a career in game writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book promises 'the best way to break into the video game industry' and includes direct experiences and tips from seasoned industry writers on getting hired.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to be an efficient part of a team
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviors and practices that make a writer a productive and valued team member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key features and multiple chapters stress collaboration, documentation, productivity techniques, and communication as essential to working effectively within teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical writing advice and effective writing tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete technical-writing best practices and concise tips for producing usable game text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description highlights 'technical writing advice' and 'effective writing tips' — guidance aimed at clarity, concision, and implementability across tutorial text, UI, and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions for innovation in game narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies and examples for pushing narrative beyond common conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book includes chapters and essays ('If It Works, Break It') that offer suggestions for innovating in game narrative while being mindful of player experience and production realities.
